summary: First test pass of the admin-only /reverse-engineer (REA) ORA chat skill. Backend: 18/19 new pytest cases pass (gating 401/403, SSRF 400 on literal private hosts, 409 concurrency, 404s, job doc hides file_text_by_sha256 and _id, live example.com round trip in ~11-13s with real '<title>Example Domain</title>' HTML). Frontend: admin flow fully works on /dashboard (slash autocomplete shows item, Enter + Send button both work, card goes from analyzing to a 2-pane file list ('/' 577 B, '/s.js' 1.5 KB), clicking a file renders real HTML in CodeBlock, backend_note shown, observed-endpoints section correctly omitted, 409 and SSRF toasts show). Non-admin: item hidden for '/' and '/rev', manual send shows 'This command is admin only.' toast, and no /admin/rea request fires. Found 1 HIGH security issue (SSRF via HTTP redirect, confirmed end to end), 1 visible UI bug (date separator reads '26 November 58783'), plus a few minor issues.

critical.issue: SSRF bypass through redirects. validate_target_url only checks the first hostname. ext_client follows redirects by default (follow_redirects=True) and nothing re-checks each hop. Reproduced: analyze url='https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/healthz' gives status=done, and the file endpoint returns the INTERNAL backend's /api/healthz JSON body. Headless Chrome also follows the redirect and can load private subresources (cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, Mongo/Redis HTTP ports and so on). Fix: in _fetch_text_resource, pass follow_redirects=False and follow hops by hand, running _is_safe_host on each Location (cap at about 5 hops). For Chrome, check the final page URL and resource URLs and drop any non-safe host, or block private ranges with --host-resolver-rules / a proxy.

minor.issue: 'ftp://example.com' is not rejected. The scheme regex fails, so the code prepends https:// and gets 'https://ftp://example.com'. The hostname then becomes 'ftp', and _is_safe_host('ftp') returns True. _is_safe_host also returns True for hosts that don't resolve ('nonexistent.invalid'), so it fails open. Reject any input that already contains '://' with a non-http(s) scheme before prepending.

A job stuck at status='running' blocks that admin with 409 forever, because nothing ever marks it stale. This happens when the backend restarts or hot-reloads mid-job (asyncio.create_task dies with the process). Add a staleness cutoff, e.g. treat running jobs older than JOB_OVERALL_TIMEOUT_S + 60s as failed, or reap them on startup. The check-then-insert is also non-atomic (two fast POSTs can both pass); a partial unique index on {requested_by, status:'running'} would fix that.
The terminal doc overwrites created_at with the finish time, so created_at == finished_at in every completed job. Drop created_at from the final $set.

The asyncio.create_task result is not stored anywhere, and the event loop only keeps a weak reference, so the task can be garbage-collected. Keep it in a module-level set and discard it in a done callback.

ui_bugs.issue: Both new messages use ts: Date.now() (milliseconds), but every other chat message uses Date.now()/1000 (seconds). The date separator above the REA messages renders as '26 November 58783'. Fix: ts: Date.now() / 1000 for both messages.

integration_issues.issue: The rea_job messages exist only in local React state and are never saved to chat history, so the card is gone after a reload or chat switch. db.rea_jobs keeps the result, but the UI has no way to reopen it. Consider persisting the message, or adding a 'recent REA jobs' list.

issues: Minified single-line HTML wraps into a short CodeBlock (about 4 visible lines) while the pane has min-height 220px, leaving a large empty gap below the code. Give the code viewer a fixed or min height (e.g. 320px) inside the card.

The backend_note and the code placeholder have no data-testid. Suggest adding 'rea-backend-note' and 'rea-code-placeholder' (I could not add them because file edits outside tests were blocked by the harness).

action_items: HIGH: Close the SSRF-via-redirect hole in rea_service (_fetch_text_resource with follow_redirects=False plus a manual per-hop _is_safe_host check; also guard Chrome's final URL and subresources).
Fix validate_target_url so it rejects non-http(s) schemes like ftp:// instead of prepending https://.
Fix ts: Date.now() -> Date.now()/1000 in runReverseEngineerCommand (bogus year 58783 date separator).
Add a stale-running-job cutoff so a restart mid-job does not 409-lock the admin forever.
Don't overwrite created_at in the terminal job doc; keep a strong reference to the background task.
Optional: persist the rea_job chat message, enlarge the code pane, add data-testids rea-backend-note / rea-code-placeholder.
critical_code_review_comments: Router admin gating via router-level Depends(require_admin_dep) is correct; GET routes are gated too (non-admin gets 403).
The GET job projection correctly excludes _id and file_text_by_sha256.

The toast in runReverseEngineerCommand shows e.response.data.detail raw. For a 422, detail is an array, so it bypasses sanitizeErrorMessage and could render an object. Wrap it with sanitizeErrorMessage.
The React list key is f.sha256. Two captured files with identical content give duplicate keys and duplicate data-testids.

success_rate.backend: 95% (18/19; the 1 failure is a real validator bug: ftp:// accepted)
success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows pass; the ts/date bug is cosmetic)

test_credentials: test@aurem.dev / AuremTest2026! (founder). Throwaway non-admin signups test_rea_nonadmin_*@example.com / test_rea_ui_*@example.com.
seed_data_creation: A few rea_jobs docs for test_admin_001 (example.com x3, plus the httpbin redirect SSRF repro job rea_dc7c3a03cd4b). Throwaway non-admin dev_users created by pytest and UI tests.
flaky_tests: Once (1 of 3 dashboard loads), the /dashboard reload right after a REA job showed the 'Something went wrong loading this page' error boundary. It did not reproduce on 2 more loads; most likely a transient chunk/network hiccup, not REA-specific.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin chat lives at /dashboard (ChatPanel). Log in through the API and set localStorage aurem_token + aurem_user (JSON with is_admin/tier). Node22/rea is already installed at /opt/node22; an example.com job takes about 11-13s. The pytest file runs the live round trip and needs no running job for test_admin_001, otherwise it skips. For the SSRF retest use https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/healthz: after the fix it must not return the internal healthz JSON.
rca of the issue: SSRF: validate_target_url only validates the hostname the user typed. Both fetch paths (httpx through ext_client with follow_redirects=True, and headless Chromium) then follow server-side redirects without re-validating, so a public redirector can reach loopback or private targets. Year 58783: messages are created with millisecond timestamps where the rest of ChatPanel expects seconds, so the separator multiplies by 1000 again.
